company_name: Rio Tinto plc (NYSE ADR, 1 ADR = 1 plc ordinary share)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Volume-led mid-cycle judgment, not a CAGR: guided copper-equivalent production growth ~3%/yr to 2030 (Simandou to 60Mtpa Simfer share, Oyu Tolgoi to 500kt 2028-36, lithium to ~200ktpa LCE by 2028, Pilbara replacement mines 2027) plus ~1-2% nominal price drift, net of a FY2027 price reversion. Cross-checked against revenue 5-yr CAGR 5.3% (FY2020 -> FY2025, trough-ish to mid-cycle) and equity 5-yr CAGR 5.7%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (7.4% / 5.7%) diverges >30% from EPS CAGR (-7.2% / +0.3%) and from 3-yr revenue (1.2%). Every 3-year series starts in FY2022, the back half of the FY2021-22 iron-ore boom; equity is inflated by the FY2025 Arcadium acquisition (share-funded NCI contributions and retained earnings at a 50-60% payout); EPS is bent by impairments and the FY2024 consolidation gain. None is a usable growth anchor for a price-taking commodity producer, so the forward path is built from guided volumes and a mid-cycle price deck.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC; no interest strip because net debt) went 9,548 (FY2020) -> 17,835 (FY2021 peak) -> 9,262 / 7,930 / 5,806 / 4,260 (FY2022-25). The -14.9% 5-yr CAGR is a mid-cycle-to-capex-peak comparison: capex rose from 6.2bn (FY2020) to 12.3bn (FY2025, Simandou + Oyu Tolgoi underground + Arcadium) while underlying EBITDA was flat at 23-25bn, not deterioration of the asset base. Owner-FCF CAGR (-14.9%) is modestly below reported (-14.2%) because SBC grew 138 -> 237 over the period. The 10-year average owner FCF FY2016-25 is ~8.4bn.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle: commodity prices revert from H1 2026's copper-, gold- and aluminium-led record toward a deck Rio actually earned FY2025's 44% margin on (iron ore ~US$95/t, copper ~US$9,500-10,000/t, aluminium ~US$2,600/t); Simandou ramps to 60Mtpa Simfer share by 2028-29, Oyu Tolgoi climbs toward 500kt/yr, the three Argentine lithium projects reach ~200ktpa LCE and turn EBITDA-positive; Pilbara is a flat ~325-335Mt cash engine on a ~1bn t China steel plateau; the ~US$11bn capex cycle steps down to ~US$10bn real from 2028 and ~US$1bn/yr of rehabilitation cash keeps flowing out below EBITDA; the US$1.8bn productivity run-rate roughly offsets cost inflation. Weighted at 50%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Copper supercycle: structural electrification, grid and AI data-centre demand hold copper at US$11-12k/t and lithium above US$20k/t, China steel stays resilient enough for iron ore to hold US$100+/t with Simandou's 65% Fe earning its grade premium, aluminium stays tight; Oyu Tolgoi, Simandou and Rincon all deliver on schedule and the US$5-10bn divestment program recycles capital into Resolution/Winu/La Granja; margins settle around 50% and the market pays ~5.5x EBITDA at exit. Weighted at 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: China rolls over as Simandou floods the market: steel output declines, Simandou plus Pilbara create a 100Mt+ seaborne surplus and iron ore settles at US$70-80/t, cannibalising Rio's own Pilbara economics; copper softens to ~US$8,000/t and lithium relapses; Mongolia renegotiates Oyu Tolgoi's fiscal terms and the Guinea partnership frictions slow the ramp; the committed capex program is sticky while revenue falls 15%, margins sit in the high-30s and the exit multiple compresses to ~4.3x EBITDA. Weighted at 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A price-taking diversified miner is valued on what its asset base earns through the cycle, not on the deck at the top of it. The build starts from a TTM that includes the strongest half-year since 2021, pulls FY2027 back to a mid-cycle deck Rio actually earned FY2025's margin on, lets guided volumes (Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi, lithium) carry the growth, charges the US$11bn capex cycle and the ~US$1bn/yr rehabilitation outflow explicitly, hands the NCI partners their share through a leakage rate rather than a book-value deduction, and caps the exit at the bottom of Rio's own historical EV/EBITDA range. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and a 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate. At US$94 the market is paying for something close to the H1 2026 deck; the value here is what is left if it reverts.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity deck: every US$10/t on iron ore is ~US$3bn of EBITDA on ~300Mt attributable shipments (~US$1.2bn of owner FCF after tax/NCI, ~US$9/share at 15x); every US$1,000/t on copper ~US$0.9bn EBITDA at ~900kt and rising. The base/bull/bear spread is almost entirely this.
Simandou execution and iron ore oversupply: Rio is adding the supply that pressures its own Pilbara price; a slower ramp protects price but delays the volume growth in the base path.
Oyu Tolgoi fiscal terms: a larger Mongolian economic share (tax assessments, Investment Agreement renegotiation) would raise the leakage rate above the 38% assumed from FY2031.
Capex overrun or extension beyond ~US$10bn real from 2028: each US$1bn/yr of extra capex in perpetuity is ~US$8/share.
Terminal cap: 15x terminal FCF (~5.1x EBITDA) binds; at 14x the base falls ~US$3/share, at Gordon (15.7x) it rises ~US$2.
Closure provisions: charged as ~US$1.0bn/yr in perpetuity; the US$18.9bn stock implies the run-rate could rise as legacy sites (ERA Ranger, Gove, Argyle) move into active rehabilitation.
Corporate action: the abandoned Glencore merger shows appetite for transformative deals; a renewed approach would break the three-scenario frame.
FX: costs are AUD/CAD-heavy against USD revenue; a weaker USD was a ~US$0.7bn EBITDA headwind in H1 2026 alone.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (query1.finance.yahoo.com, RIO) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 65.35-112.58.
data_sources.financials: RIO_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2012-H1 2026) and the FY2025 Annual Report on Form 20-F (consolidated income statement, cash flow statement, underlying-EBITDA reconciliation, note 14 closure provisions, note 13 PP&E); H1 2026 results release (29 July 2026): net-debt table, share-count note, 'Rio Tinto share of capital investment' reconciliation, income statement and NCI lines.
data_sources.qualitative: RIO_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): segments, guidance (shipments 343-366Mt, capex ~US$11bn 2026-27 and ~US$10bn from 2028, US$1.8bn productivity run-rate, US$5-10bn divestments, Oyu Tolgoi 500kt 2028-36, lithium ~200ktpa LCE by 2028), bull/bear cases, Glencore talks, Mongolia tax dispute, Kennecott furnace breach.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: TTM to 30 June 2026 = H2 FY2025 (57,638 - 26,873 = 30,765) + H1 2026 (31,028). The TTM is used as FY0 so the flows start from the same date as the balance-sheet anchors (30-Jun-2026): Y1 is therefore the twelve months to mid-2027 (~FY2027), discounted one full year from the October 2026 valuation date. Using FY2025 as FY0 with the June balance sheet would double count H1 2026 cash flow; using the December 2025 balance sheet would credit a buyer today with the US$6.0bn of FY2025-final and 2026-interim dividends already paid.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow add-back (core_metrics StockBasedComp 237; FY2024 172, FY2023 144). Awards are satisfied with shares bought on market by the employee share trusts, so there is no separate net-share-settlement tax outflow to add; no combined figure is published, so the add-back is used as-is.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 actual, last completed fiscal year: reported FCF 4,497 (OCF 16,832 - PP&E and intangibles 12,335, the CSV definition) - SBC 237 = 4,260 owner FCF. Interest income NOT stripped: the group is net debt and the build starts from underlying EBITDA, which excludes finance income. TTM to Jun-2026 on the same basis: OCF 19,081 - capex 13,548 - SBC 237 = 5,296; on Rio's own definition (less Rio share of capital investment 11,859 and lease principal 589) TTM FCF is ~6,400, or ~8,000 unlevered before net interest paid (~1,060).
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and quote are all USD; no conversion. The NYSE ADR is 1:1 with a Rio Tinto plc ordinary share (not an ADS ratio like BHP's 2:1), so per-share values here are per ADR. Parity check: RIO.L GBp quote x GBPUSD and RIO.AX AUD quote x AUDUSD should both land within ~1-2% of the ADR after the time-zone gap.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the TTM to 30 June 2026 standing in for calendar FY2026 (Dec year-end). Y1 = FY2027 ... Y10 = FY2036.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Friday session; Saturday valuation date, not an after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 1,255.0m Rio Tinto plc + 371.8m Rio Tinto Limited ordinary shares in issue and held by the public at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 2026 results, EPS note) = 1,626.8m basic, plus ~14m dilutive employee awards (FY2025 diluted WASO 1,638.0 vs basic 1,624.0; core_metrics H1-2026 diluted 1,640.2) = 1,641m. Held FLAT: SBC (0.4% of revenue) is expensed in the flows and awards are satisfied with shares the trusts buy on market. No buyback since 2020 (US$208m); the flat count is a convention the company funds through trust purchases, not a repurchase program. DLC structure: plc and Limited shares carry identical economic rights, so the combined count is the divisor.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Ex-lease net debt at 30-Jun-2026 from the H1 2026 net-debt table: borrowings excl. overdrafts 21,414 + derivatives related to net debt 263 = total_debt 21,677; cash 8,913 + other liquid investments 141 = cash 9,054; net debt 12,623. Rio's own net debt of 14,061 includes lease liabilities 1,438, which are EXCLUDED here because leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B). The Oyu Tolgoi carried-interest loan receivable from Erdenes (Mongolia's 34%, repaid out of its dividend share) is NOT added as an asset; it offsets the day-one NCI leakage on Oyu Tolgoi, which in cash terms accrues to Rio until the loan is repaid.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-built, matching the flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 (diversified tier-one miner, somewhat more iron-ore-concentrated than BHP's 0.95) -> cost of equity ~9.2%; pre-tax debt cost ~5.3% (A-rated), ~3.7% after tax, at ~12% of capital (total debt 21.7bn vs market cap ~155bn) -> WACC ~8.5%. No country, commodity or Mongolia/Guinea premium: cyclicality, China concentration and sovereign risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, once (adaptations 7f). Same WACC in every scenario. Identical to the BHP build so the two diversified miners are comparable.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash payment (principal 522 FY2025 / 589 TTM to Jun-2026, plus ~US$75m lease interest at ~5% on ~1.5bn of liabilities) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path 1.1% of mid-cycle revenue; D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (~450/yr on 1,421 of ROU assets) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT; ALL lease liabilities (1,438 at 30-Jun-2026) excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: the NCI share (Simfer/Simandou 47% CIOH, Oyu Tolgoi 34% Erdenes, IOC 41%, Richards Bay 26%, ERA ~14%) is folded into the combined cash tax + NCI leakage driver; NO NCI deduction in the bridge (NCI equity 6,239 at 30-Jun-2026 is mostly CIOH's capital contributions to Simfer at cost). Capex is on the 'Rio Tinto share of capital investment' basis (PP&E purchases + EAU funding - partner cash calls - PP&E sales; 5,037 H1 2026 vs 5,947 gross), so partners fund their share of Simfer capex and the leakage removes their share of profit: consistent with the BHP build. Calibration: FY2025 income tax 4,319 + EAU tax and finance 1,514 = 5,833 on EBIT (underlying EBITDA 25,363 - subs D&A 6,271 - EAU D&A 594 = 18,498) = 31.5%; NCI profit 283 FY2025 (1.5%) but 530 in H1 2026 alone (Oyu Tolgoi at record copper), TTM ~805 (~3.9% of EBIT). Leakage path therefore starts at 34.5% (31% tax + 3.5% NCI) and rises to 38% by Y5 as Simandou (47% NCI) reaches 60Mtpa and Oyu Tolgoi (34% NCI) ramps to 500kt. FY0 check on TTM: underlying earnings 12,912 + after-tax net finance cost and provision-discount unwind (~1,000) - after-tax lease interest (~55) = ~13,850 attributable unlevered NOPAT vs model EBIT ~20,600 -> 32.8% leakage, below the Y1 34.5% because H1 2026's 25.2% effective tax rate (deferred-tax re-recognition at Tomago and US CAMT) was a one-off.
inputs.eau_treatment: Underlying EBITDA includes Rio's share of equity-accounted units' EBITDA (Escondida 30%, WCS rail/port, etc.: 1,478 profit + 594 D&A + 1,514 tax/finance = 3,586 FY2025, ~14% of group EBITDA) while the cash arrives as dividends (1,070). To treat that share as if consolidated: EAU D&A is inside da_pct_path, EAU tax inside the leakage driver, and ~1.0pp of revenue (~US$0.6bn Rio-share Escondida sustaining capex, self-funded inside Escondida and therefore absent from 'Rio share of capital investment') is added to capex_pct_path. WCS infrastructure funding is already in the capital-investment measure.
inputs.closure_treatment: Closure/rehabilitation cash spend is charged IN THE FLOWS, not in the bridge. Utilisation of close-down provisions (1,049 FY2025, 1,142 FY2024, 777 FY2023; 3-yr avg 989) sits in OCF below EBITDA (the provision charge is capitalised and depreciated), so an EBITDA-built FCF misses it. ~1.7% of mid-cycle revenue (~US$1.0bn/yr) is deducted from every scenario's EBITDA margin path in perpetuity, because Rio continuously closes and rehabilitates sites. Consequently the 18,882 closure provision stock (17,667 non-current + 1,215 current at 30-Jun-2026) is NOT deducted in the bridge: that would charge the same cash twice. This is more complete than the BHP build (which deducted only closed-site provisions at stock) and ~US$1bn/yr more conservative on the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the cyclical, lease, NCI and excluded-income adaptations. Rio Tinto is a mature diversified miner (iron ore ~47% of revenue, copper ~24%, aluminium ~24%, lithium/other ~5%; copper + aluminium + lithium >50% of H1 2026 EBITDA for the first time) whose cash flows are a real operating stream, so owner-FCF is the right engine; the cyclicality is handled by building FY2027 off a mid-cycle commodity deck rather than the TTM, which embeds record H1 2026 copper, gold and aluminium prices. Fresh build: no prior Drivers/DCF, no MEMORY entry. Comparable: BHP (Drivers 2026-10-03) uses the same engine, WACC 8.5%, 10-year horizon, treatment-B leases, NCI-as-leakage; this build adopts the same frame and differs where Rio's facts differ (lower structural margin because of aluminium, higher capex intensity through the Simandou/Oyu Tolgoi/lithium cycle, closure cash charged in the flows). NORMALISATION: (1) Underlying EBITDA (CSV EBITDA column) is the base, so impairments (341 FY2025), the FY2024 1,214 consolidation gain, embedded-derivative marks and closure re-estimates for impaired sites are outside the flows; (2) TTM underlying margin 46.4% (H1 2026 47.8%) is above the FY2022-FY2025 range of 43.4-47.3% (avg 44.7%), and FY2025's 44.0% was earned on roughly the mid-cycle deck assumed here (iron ore ~US$100/t, copper ~US$9,500/t, aluminium ~US$2,600/t), so base runs 44.4-45.4% pre-SBC before closure, i.e. 42.7-43.7% as entered (after the 1.7pp closure charge) and ~42.3-43.3% post-SBC; (3) Y1 (FY2027) revenue is set 5% below the TTM: ~-8 to -9% from price normalisation (iron ore ~US$95/t vs ~US$100-105 in 2026, copper ~US$9,500-10,000 vs US$11-12k in H1 2026, aluminium ~US$2,600) partly offset by +3-4% volume (Simandou ramp, Oyu Tolgoi underground, Rincon/Fenix/Sal de Vida lithium, Pilbara replacement mines) -> ~US$58.7bn, between FY2025's 57.6bn and the TTM; (4) the ~US$11bn capex cycle (2026-27 guidance, ~US$10bn real from 2028, sustaining ~US$4bn) is carried explicitly on the Rio-share basis plus ~1pp for Escondida's self-funded capex, tapering to 16% of revenue by FY2034 against D&A at 13% (1.23x, the reinvestment that funds 2% terminal growth in a depleting business rather than assuming it for free). SBC is expensed at 0.4% of revenue and the EBITDA path is grossed up by the same 0.4pp because IFRS underlying EBITDA is already post-SBC (charged once). SBC-near-zero: house and street differ by well under US$1/share; read band_position as n/a. BRIDGE: ex-lease net debt only; no equity_bridge items (closure in flows, NCI in leakage, OT carried loan not added, Escondida inside the flows). PRICE DEPENDENCE: at US$94 the market is capitalising something close to the H1 2026 commodity deck; the base case says that deck is above mid-cycle.

bear.rationale: China rolls over and Simandou floods the market: steel output declines 2-3%/yr, Simandou's 120Mtpa system plus Pilbara pushes the seaborne surplus to 100Mt+ and iron ore settles at US$70-80/t; copper softens to ~US$8,000/t as the AI/grid build-out slows; aluminium US$2,300; lithium relapses below US$10k/t and Arcadium stays cash-negative. FY2027 revenue -15% (~US$52.5bn, between FY2019's 43bn and FY2020's 45bn in real terms), -3% in FY2028, then volume-only growth. Entered margin 37-38.5% = ~39-40.6% underlying pre-closure, FY2016-18's 40-46% at US$55-70/t iron ore less the aluminium/lithium drag. Capex is sticky at the committed ~US$11bn for 2027 (21% of the lower revenue) and only eases to US$10bn from 2028; D&A and leases are fixed in dollars so they rise as a share. Mongolia extracts a larger share of Oyu Tolgoi, offset by a lower NCI profit share: leakage 36%. Exit 12x FCF (~4.3x EBITDA), g 1.5%.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2027 -5% on the TTM: price reversion from record H1 2026 copper/gold/aluminium to a mid-cycle deck (iron ore ~US$95/t CFR, copper ~US$9,500-10,000/t, aluminium ~US$2,600/t, lithium carbonate ~US$12-15k/t) worth roughly -8 to -9%, offset by +3-4% volume (Simandou first full year of shipments at ~20-30Mt system, Oyu Tolgoi underground panels, Rincon/Fenix 1B/Sal de Vida first production, Pilbara flat at 323-338Mt). Lands at ~US$58.7bn: above FY2025's 57.6bn because volumes are higher, below the TTM 61.8bn because prices are lower. FY2028-30 +4%: Simandou ramps to 60Mtpa Simfer (consolidated 100%), Oyu Tolgoi toward 500kt, lithium to ~200ktpa LCE, Brockman Syncline 1 / Hope Downs 2 / West Angelas replace depleting Pilbara pits; ~2% nominal price drift. Fades to 2.5% by FY2034-36 as the sanctioned pipeline matures and Pilbara volumes plateau.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: ENTERED FIGURE = pre-SBC underlying EBITDA margin MINUS 1.7pp of closure/rehabilitation cash spend (see inputs.closure_treatment). Underlying (post-SBC, pre-closure) ~44.0% FY2027 rising to ~45.0% from FY2029 as copper grows in the mix and the US$1.8bn productivity run-rate (reached end-2026) offsets cost inflation: inside the FY2022-FY2025 range of 43.4-47.3%, equal to FY2025's 44.0% earned on roughly this deck, below the TTM 46.4% and H1 2026's 47.8%, and far below FY2020-21's 53.6-59.4%. Lithium (negative EBITDA in 2025-26) turning positive from 2027-28 is part of the +1pp.
base.da_pct_path_rationale: Subsidiaries D&A ex capitalised depreciation 7,232 TTM + EAU share ~620 - right-of-use depreciation ~450 = ~7,400 = 12.0% of TTM revenue, 12.6% of the lower FY2027 mid-cycle revenue; rising to 13.0% as ~US$20bn of Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi underground, Rincon and Western Range assets are commissioned 2026-28.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: 'Rio Tinto share of capital investment' basis (PP&E + intangibles + EAU funding - partner cash calls - disposals: 11,326 FY2025 restated, ~11,860 TTM) plus ~1.0pp of revenue for Rio's 30% share of Escondida's self-funded sustaining capex so the EAU EBITDA inside the base carries its own capex. Guidance: up to ~US$11bn in 2026 and 2027, ~US$10bn (real 2025) from 2028, sustaining ~US$4bn. FY2027 ~11.0bn + 0.6 = 19.7% of 58.7bn; FY2028 ~10.5 + 0.6 = 18.2%; nominal ~10.7-11.3bn through FY2031 (Simandou complete, Oyu Tolgoi Hugo North Lift 1 panels, Rincon full-scale, lithium hydroxide decision, Pilbara replacement mines, Resolution/Winu studies), then tapering to 16% of revenue (~US$12.5bn by FY2036) vs D&A ex-ROU at 13%: a 1.23x reinvestment ratio that funds 2% terminal growth in a depleting business.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: Combined leakage on EBIT: ~31% income tax (Australia 30% + royalties in opex, Mongolia 25%, Canada ~26%, Guinea 30%, US 21%+state; FY2025 subsidiaries 4,319 + EAU 1,514 = 31.5% of EBIT) plus the NCI share of profit, 3.5% in FY2027 rising to ~7% by FY2031 as Simandou (47% CIOH) and Oyu Tolgoi (34% Erdenes) become the growth engines. See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_capture_rationale: Producer: receivables + inventories exceed payables; growth consumes cash and contraction releases it (FY2025 WC outflow 244 on a +4.0bn revenue move, FY2023 outflow 926 on a -1.5bn move with inventory build; FY2024 inflow on flat revenue). -10% of the revenue change is a mid-point that keeps the FY2027 release modest (~+0.3bn) and charges ~0.2bn/yr through the growth years.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 15x terminal owner FCF binds below Gordon (8.5%/2.0% = 15.7x). Terminal FCF/EBITDA conversion is ~34% (capex 1.23x D&A, closure and leases charged), so 15x FCF is only ~5.1x terminal EBITDA, the bottom of Rio's through-cycle 5-7x EV/EBITDA range and below today's ~5.8x on TTM EBITDA. The low end of the 12-15x cyclical band would double-penalise a terminal FCF that is already mid-cycle with growth capex normalised; 15x is the top of the band for that reason, one notch above BHP's 14x because Rio's conversion is lower and the EBITDA-equivalent would otherwise fall to ~4.8x. Bull 16x (~5.5x EBITDA), bear 12x (~4.3x).

bull.rationale: Copper supercycle plus iron ore holding: copper US$11-12k/t on electrification/AI-power demand, iron ore US$100-110/t as China steel plateaus near 1bn t and Simandou's high grade earns its premium, aluminium US$2,900+ with tariff-driven regional premiums. FY2027 revenue flat on the TTM (price holds, volume grows), then 5-6% as Simandou, Oyu Tolgoi and lithium all deliver on schedule and lithium prices stay above US$20k/t. Entered margin 48-49% = ~49.7-50.7% underlying pre-closure, i.e. H1 2026's 47.8% plus two years of the productivity program, within FY2019-20's 49-54%. NCI leakage higher (38.5%) because Simandou and Oyu Tolgoi are the most profitable assets in this case. Exit 16x FCF (~5.5x EBITDA), g 2.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above BHP's 20%): iron ore is ~47% of revenue versus BHP's ~38%, Simandou's ramp is itself the mechanism of the bear case (Rio is the one adding the supply), and two of the three growth engines sit in jurisdictions with live fiscal disputes (Mongolia's US$443m assessment and Investment Agreement pressure; Guinea), so the downside is both margin compression and a real sovereign tail, though 16% gearing and first-quartile Pilbara costs keep it short of solvency. Base 50%: mid-cycle deck with guided volumes. Bull 25%: copper is now the single largest EBITDA contributor and carries a broadly held structural-deficit thesis, but the bull case also needs China steel to hold, lithium to stay above US$20k/t and three flagship projects to ramp on time, several independent things going right, so it is trimmed from the house 35% and held equal to the bear.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: Read band_position as n/a. SBC is 0.4% of revenue, so house and street differ by well under US$1/share and (price - house)/(street - house) is degenerate (the build recomputes the field). The price sits far above BOTH bases: the gap is a commodity-deck question, not an SBC-accounting one.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
